summary: MO-046 Founder Beta Production Readiness (Developer vs Founder Mode). 24/24 backend pytest cases PASSED. Frontend: 23 connectors visible, Founder-Mode hides ALL developer credentials (verified: no 'Client ID', 'Client Secret', or 'Redirect URI' anywhere in body), 17 setup notes for OAuth connectors, Developer-Mode toggle works, devconfig dialog opens with pre-filled backend redirect_uri, saving dummy config transitions github to 'Needs Authorization', Founder-mode then reveals Connect button, Test Connection opens test-result-dialog with checks, cleanup restores 'Developer Setup Required'. All 11 nav routes render without crash. Evidence metric-card-connector_status shows LIVE 2/23 Operational Connectors. Bad-state OAuth callback redirects to /connectors and toasts error. Production status vocabulary confirmed — only 'Connected', 'Developer Setup Required', 'Needs Authorization', 'Ready to Publish' seen; NO legacy 'Connected Healthy' / 'Setup Required' / 'Developer Configuration Required'. Cleaned up: deleted github developer-config after tests. Two minor bugs found (see below).

ui_bugs.issue: In Developer Mode, api_key connectors (woocommerce, amazon_kdp, tpt, shopify) do NOT show a 'Developer Setup' button. Root cause: the render condition is `{devMode && c.oauth_supported !== false && (...)}` — for api_key connectors backend returns oauth_supported=false, so the button is filtered out. The spec (feature #5) explicitly requires that clicking Developer Setup on an api_key connector like woocommerce opens the connect-dialog with connect-apikey-input. Currently there is NO way for the admin to open the API-key dialog in Developer Mode. Fix: change condition to `{devMode && (c.auth_method !== 'oauth' || c.oauth_supported !== false) && (...)}` OR simply `{devMode && (...)}` — the branching by auth_method inside onClick already handles routing.

ui_bugs.component: Connectors.js — disabled Publish tooltip for stripe
ui_bugs.issue: `connector-publish-disabled-stripe` has NO title tooltip (empty). Backend `publish_disabled_reason` returns None because stripe is operational=true AND connected=true, but stripe capabilities don't include 'publish' so can_publish=false. Every disabled Publish button MUST expose a reason per the requirement. Fix: in connectors.py _public, add a branch for operational+connected connectors that lack 'publish' capability (e.g. stripe): 'Stripe handles pricing & checkout automatically for QRU Store™ products — it isn't a standalone publish target.'

action_items: Fix Connectors.js gate: allow api_key connectors to show `connector-devconfig-<id>` button in Developer Mode (currently only shown when oauth_supported !== false).
Fix connectors.py `_public.publish_disabled_reason`: return a non-null reason for stripe (and any operational connector lacking the 'publish' capability) so the tooltip is never blank.
critical_code_review_comments: Connectors.js line 149: `{devMode && c.oauth_supported !== false && (...)` — this render gate breaks the universal lifecycle for api_key connectors. Consider decoupling the gate from oauth_supported and letting auth_method determine which dialog to open (as the onClick already does).

connectors.py _public: `publish_disabled_reason` computed as (operational + connected -> None). This assumes operational=True means 'has publish capability', which is false for stripe. Reason should be derived per-capability instead of per-operational-flag.

Founder-Mode `connector-setup-note-<id>` is only rendered when `c.oauth_supported !== false`. This means api_key connectors (woocommerce, amazon_kdp, tpt, shopify) with status 'Developer Setup Required' show NO explanatory note to the Founder — the founder sees a bare status chip. Consider showing the same note for any non-configured connector regardless of auth method.
23 connectors on one page is a lot; consider grouping by category in Founder view or adding a search/filter (minor UX).

Founder-Mode devMode is client-side state only — an admin could bypass the toggle via devtools; backend already enforces super-admin on developer-config endpoints so this is defense-in-depth, but worth documenting.

bug1_api_key_devconfig_hidden.reproduction: Login as Founder → /connectors → click Developer Mode toggle ON → look at woocommerce/shopify/amazon_kdp/tpt cards. NO connector-devconfig-<id> button appears. Spec requires clicking Developer Setup on woocommerce (api_key) opens the connect-dialog.
bug1_api_key_devconfig_hidden.rca: Connectors.js line 149 render gate: `{devMode && c.oauth_supported !== false && ...}`. Backend _public sets oauth_supported=false for api_key connectors. This gate correctly hides devconfig for connectors that don't support OAuth, but api_key connectors DO need their own developer-setup flow (API key entry). The gate is over-broad.
bug1_api_key_devconfig_hidden.mitigation: Change gate to `{devMode && (c.auth_method === 'oauth' ? c.oauth_supported !== false : true) && ...}` OR simply `{devMode && c.auth_method !== 'native' && ...}` — the onClick already handles which dialog to open.

bug2_stripe_disabled_publish_no_tooltip.reproduction: Login → /connectors → hover stripe's disabled Publish button → no tooltip appears. `connector-publish-disabled-stripe` has empty title attribute.
bug2_stripe_disabled_publish_no_tooltip.rca: connectors.py _public.publish_disabled_reason logic: `(None if (reg['operational'] and connected) else ...)`. Stripe is operational=True AND connected (status='Connected'), so publish_disabled_reason=None. But stripe.can_publish is False because 'publish' is not in stripe.capabilities. The reason is incorrectly gated by operational+connected instead of by can_publish.
bug2_stripe_disabled_publish_no_tooltip.mitigation: Rework `publish_disabled_reason` to be non-null whenever `can_publish` is False. Special-case stripe with a friendly message like 'Stripe handles pricing & checkout automatically for QRU Store™ products — it isn't a standalone publish target.'
